# Technology @ Stage 6 — Nominal & Rule

> developed 2026-07-24.

## Crosswalk (from unified ladder)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IST Stage# | 6 |
| Canonical name | Nominal & Rule |
| Altitude | `amber` (Ethnocentric) |
| MHC Order | 5 (Nominal) |
| Kegan | 2 |
| Identity band | Ethnocentric |

## Expression on this line

Technology at Order 5 is norm-governed tool production and craft specialization: tools are
produced according to named standards and codified procedures, and craft knowledge is organized
into specialized roles (the potter, the smith, the weaver, the builder). The key advance over
Order 4 is that tool production is no longer ad hoc and situation-specific — it follows
established rules and produces standardized outputs.

The "technology" here is the codified craft: the kiln temperature that produces the right
clay hardness, the metal alloy that produces the right blade strength, the joinery technique
that produces the right structural integrity. The craftsperson follows the rule ("this is how
we make this tool"), not just adapts to the situation. Innovation is limited to working within
the established framework; fundamental changes to the production process require a different
order of cognitive capacity.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** the felt obligation to follow the craft standard — the rule experienced as binding.
- **UR:** reliable, standardized tool production that persists across situations.
- **LL:** the shared craft culture — the named standards, roles, and rules that define proper
  production.
- **LR:** the codified craft knowledge — the technical standards, quality benchmarks, production
  procedures as external artifacts.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** craft rigidity — the production process cannot deviate from the standard
  even when the situation demands it.
- **Dark allergy:** craft absence — no standardized production process, each tool is ad hoc.
- **Golden addiction:** claiming to have designed a systematic production process (Order 6)
  when actually just following inherited rules.
- **Golden allergy:** refusing to follow craft standards because they constrain creativity.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Rule-governed production:** tools are produced according to codified standards and
  procedures.
- **Specialized craft roles:** production is organized by named craft specializations.
- **Standardized outputs:** the production process produces consistent, predictable tools.

## Sources, joints, open questions

**Sources:** Adamson, *The Craft Reader* (craft as norm-governed practice); Sennett,
*The Craftsman* (craft knowledge as codified practice); Polanyi, *The Tacit Dimension*
(craft knowledge as both explicit and tacit).
**Open joints:** What determines the transition from norm-governed craft (Order 5) to
deliberate innovation and design (Order 6)?
**Research debt:** pairs with `05-sensory-motor` (flexible tool adaptation) and
`07-sentential-faith` (craft knowledge as tradition).
